Design secure access to AWS resources; design secure workloads and applications; determine appropriate data security controls. Tasks include selecting access control mechanisms across accounts and roles (for example AWS Organizations, SCPs, federated directory services, IAM roles), securing application endpoints, managing ports/protocols/network traffic, implementing encryption/in-transit and at-rest, backups and retention policies, and aligning AWS technologies with compliance requirements.

Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures; design highly available and fault-tolerant architectures. Tasks include designing architectures using microservices/event-driven patterns, horizontal/vertical scaling, load-balancing, decoupling components (for example SQS, SNS), selecting storage types (object/file/block) appropriately, leveraging multi-AZ/multi-region for high availability and rapid fail-over.

Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions; design high-performing and elastic compute solutions; determine high-performing database solutions; design high-performing and/or scalable network architectures; determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions. Tasks include choosing compute types (EC2, Lambda, Fargate), storage types (S3, EFS, FSx), database types (RDS, DynamoDB, Aurora), network architectures (VPC endpoints, Direct Connect, Global Accelerator), and ingestion/transformation services (Glue, DataSync) to meet performance and scalability requirements.

Design cost-optimized storage solutions; design cost-optimized compute solutions; design cost-optimized database solutions; design cost-optimized network architectures. Tasks include selecting the most cost-effective service options (On-Demand vs Reserved vs Spot, Savings Plans), matching storage classes and lifecycle policies to use cases, rightsizing compute and database instances, leveraging cost monitoring/management tools, and architecting network traffic and connectivity with cost-effectiveness in mind.

Implement monitoring, logging, analysis, and remediation for AWS workloads. Tasks include configuring metrics, alarms, and filters using services like CloudWatch and CloudTrail; using the CloudWatch Agent to collect logs and metrics from EC2, ECS or EKS; creating dashboards and notifications; automating remediation via EventBridge, Systems Manager Automation run-books; and applying performance-optimization strategies across compute, storage and database services.

Ensure reliability and business continuity for AWS workloads. Tasks include designing and implementing highly available, fault-tolerant, and scalable architectures using services such as Elastic Load Balancing, Route 53 health checks, auto scaling, multi-AZ/multi-region deployments, backup and restore strategies, and disaster-recovery procedures to meet defined RTO/RPO objectives.

Automate deployment, provisioning and management of AWS resources. Tasks include managing AMIs and container images (e.g., EC2 Image Builder), deploying infrastructure as code with CloudFormation or CDK, orchestrating multi-account and multi-region deployments (e.g., StackSets, RAM), designing automated operational processes via Systems Manager and event-driven Lambda/S3 workflows, and ensuring scalable provisioning of resources.

Continuously improve existing AWS architectures by applying operational excellence principles. Enhance reliability, optimize cost and performance, implement automation for maintenance, and integrate monitoring and feedback mechanisms for ongoing improvement.

Implement security and compliance for AWS operations. Tasks include applying the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, configuring identity and access controls (e.g., IAM policies, roles, MFA), securing workloads via encryption in-transit and at-rest, enforcing compliance requirements (e.g., via Config, Security Hub, Inspector), automating remediation of findings, and applying best practices for logging, governance and audit readiness in cloud operations.

Manage networking and content delivery for performance, connectivity and availability. Tasks include configuring VPCs, subnets, route tables, NAT gateways, security groups and network ACLs; implementing private connectivity (e.g., VPN, Direct Connect); optimizing network cost and performance; configuring DNS and routing (via Route 53), content delivery (via CloudFront, Global Accelerator); trouble-shooting connectivity and analyzing logs (e.g., VPC flow logs, CloudFront logs, ELB access logs).

Optimize cost and performance in cloud operations. Tasks include applying cost-management tools (e.g., Trusted Advisor, Cost Explorer), rightsizing compute and storage resources, implementing caching and optimized database or storage configurations, automating performance tuning, and continuously analysing resource utilization and optimisation opportunities as part of operations workflows.

Develop and optimise applications on AWS. Tasks include selecting and using appropriate AWS services for application development (SDKs, APIs, CLI), implementing event-driven or serverless architectures (e.g., Lambda, API Gateway), integrating with AWS managed databases and data stores, designing application code for performance, resilience and cost-effectiveness, and packaging and deploying applications through CI/CD pipelines.

Implement security in application development on AWS. Tasks include applying the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, managing identity and access (IAM roles, federated identities, least-privilege), ensuring encryption in-transit and at-rest (e.g., KMS, SSE, TLS), implementing authentication and authorization mechanisms (e.g., Cognito, IAM policies), securing application code and data in development and deployment processes.

Deploy applications to AWS and manage their lifecycle. Tasks include using CI/CD tools (e.g., CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, CodePipeline), packaging deployment artifacts, choosing appropriate deployment strategies (all-at-once, rolling, blue/green, canary), automating resource provisioning via infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation, CDK, SAM), monitoring resource provisioning, and ensuring version control and repeatable deployments across environments.

Troubleshoot and optimise applications on AWS. Tasks include monitoring application performance and logs (e.g., CloudWatch, X-Ray, Logs Insights), diagnosing and resolving performance bottlenecks (e.g., cold starts, throttling, hot partitions), implementing caching, concurrency controls, and asynchronous messaging (e.g., DynamoDB DAX, ElastiCache, SQS, SNS), refactoring or optimizing code and infrastructure for cost, reliability and scalability.

Ingest and transform data and orchestrate data pipelines while applying programming concepts. Includes designing pipelines for streaming and batch ingestion, managing throughput and latency, merging and cleaning datasets, transforming and enriching data, scheduling and triggering jobs, and ensuring pipelines are reliable and repeatable.

Choose optimal data stores, design data models, catalogue data schemas, and manage data lifecycles. Tasks include selecting the appropriate storage (e.g., data lakes, warehouses, NoSQL vs relational), modelling schemas for analytics or operational use, managing metadata/catalogue services, and implementing lifecycle policies, versioning and archival strategies.

Operationalise, maintain, and monitor data pipelines; analyse data and ensure data quality. Covers setting up monitoring/observability for data workflows, implementing error detection and recovery, ensuring data consistency and completeness, scheduling and automating operations, and analysing pipeline performance for cost and scalability.

Implement appropriate authentication, authorization, data encryption, privacy, and governance; enable logging. This includes applying identity and access controls, key management and encryption at-rest and in-transit, managing data privacy and compliance, setting up audit logging/monitoring, and configuring governance frameworks for data in motion and rest.

Design and implement automation for the software development lifecycle (SDLC), including CI/CD pipelines, build and deployment strategies, and release management using AWS developer tools and services.

Implement configuration management and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools like AWS CloudFormation, CDK, and OpsWorks to provision, manage, and version AWS environments in a repeatable and auditable manner.

Design highly available, scalable, and self-healing cloud solutions by applying resilience strategies such as fault tolerance, automated recovery, blue/green deployments, and multi-region architectures.

Implement monitoring, observability, and logging solutions using Amazon CloudWatch, AWS X-Ray, and AWS CloudTrail to collect, visualize, and analyze metrics, logs, and traces for proactive issue detection.
Implement automated incident and event response processes using AWS services such as Lambda, Systems Manager, and EventBridge to detect, investigate, and remediate operational issues efficiently.

Implement security controls, compliance auditing, and governance automation within DevOps practices using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), AWS Config, and AWS Security Hub to enforce least privilege and compliance requirements.

Design complex multi-account, multi-VPC, and hybrid architectures that address organizational governance, scalability, and security requirements. Incorporate strategies for centralized operations, shared services, and network segmentation using AWS Organizations and Control Tower.

Design new cloud-native and hybrid solutions that meet functional, security, and compliance requirements. Select appropriate AWS services for compute, storage, database, and networking, while ensuring high availability, performance, and cost optimization.

Plan and execute workload migrations and modernizations using AWS migration tools and services. Assess existing environments, design migration strategies, automate deployments, and modernize applications with managed services and containerization.

Domain 1 (28% of exam): Ingest, transform, validate, and prepare data for ML modeling. Key competencies include: Data ingestion from diverse sources (Amazon S3, Kinesis, RDS), data transformation and cleaning using AWS Glue and SageMaker Data Wrangler, feature engineering techniques (scaling, encoding, normalization), data quality validation and bias detection using SageMaker Clarify, data annotation with SageMaker Ground Truth, and configuring data storage for training (EFS, FSx). This domain focuses on the foundational data engineering tasks required to prepare high-quality datasets for machine learning workflows.

Domain 2 (26% of exam): Select modeling approaches, train models, tune hyperparameters, analyze model performance, and manage model versions. Core areas include: Choosing appropriate ML algorithms and AWS AI services (Amazon Rekognition, Bedrock, Translate), training models using SageMaker built-in algorithms and popular frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch), hyperparameter optimization with SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning, performance analysis using metrics (F1 score, RMSE, AUC, ROC curves), model interpretation with SageMaker Clarify, and version management in SageMaker Model Registry. This domain covers the complete model development lifecycle.

topic_name: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
topic_description: Domain 3 (22% of exam): Choose deployment infrastructure and endpoints, provision compute resources, configure auto scaling, and set up CI/CD pipelines. Key responsibilities include: Selecting deployment strategies (real-time, batch, serverless), provisioning appropriate compute resources (CPU, GPU configurations), implementing auto scaling for performance optimization, setting up CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline and CodeBuild, orchestrating ML workflows with SageMaker Pipelines and Apache Airflow, and managing deployment infrastructure including containerization with ECS, EKS, and Lambda. This domain focuses on operationalizing ML models in production environments.

topic_name: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
topic_description: Domain 4 (24% of exam): Monitor models, data, and infrastructure to detect issues, optimize costs, and secure ML systems. Essential components include: Production model monitoring using SageMaker Model Monitor for performance degradation and data drift, infrastructure cost optimization with CloudWatch, Cost Explorer, and Trusted Advisor, implementing security best practices through IAM, KMS, and security groups, compliance and data protection measures, setting up monitoring dashboards and alerts, and troubleshooting ML system issues. This domain ensures the reliability, security, and cost-effectiveness of deployed ML solutions.

Design and develop scalable, resilient, and hybrid network architectures using AWS networking services. Define VPC structures, connectivity models, hybrid links, and routing strategies that meet business and performance requirements.

Implement network connectivity solutions using AWS Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, VPC peering, VPN, and Cloud WAN. Configure routing, DNS, and load balancing to ensure reliable, performant, and secure connectivity across environments.

Monitor, operate, and optimize AWS and hybrid networks using tools such as CloudWatch, VPC Flow Logs, and Network Manager. Troubleshoot connectivity issues, tune network performance, and apply automation for operational efficiency.

Secure network architectures through segmentation, encryption, and access controls. Implement compliance and governance controls using AWS Firewall Manager, Network Firewall, WAF, and IAM to ensure adherence to organizational and regulatory standards.

Detect, analyze, and respond to security threats using AWS-native tools such as GuardDuty, Detective, and Security Hub. Implement incident response plans, automate threat containment, and perform post-incident analysis to improve resilience.

Design and implement centralized security logging and continuous monitoring using AWS CloudTrail, CloudWatch, Config, and SIEM integrations. Ensure visibility into user activity, configuration changes, and network access across accounts.

Secure compute, storage, and network infrastructure by applying defense-in-depth principles. Configure network segmentation, encryption, and secure access to EC2, VPC, and containerized workloads to protect against external and internal threats.

Manage authentication, authorization, and federation using AWS IAM, AWS SSO, and identity providers. Apply the principle of least privilege, enforce MFA, manage temporary credentials, and audit access across accounts and workloads.

Protect sensitive data at rest and in transit through encryption, tokenization, and key management using AWS KMS, CloudHSM, and Secrets Manager. Design data classification and lifecycle protection strategies aligned with compliance standards.

Establish and enforce governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) frameworks using AWS Organizations, Control Tower, and Audit Manager. Align security policies with organizational goals, implement compliance reporting, and maintain continuous assurance.
